title: SentinelAI Anomaly Event
description: Published by the AI Engine to the Web Platform. Carries no model identity (spec §3.3).

occurred_at.description: When the anomaly happened, as Unix epoch seconds (UTC, fractional). Comparable across process restarts and across cameras, whatever kind of source each camera runs: sort and display on this field. Derived from a wall+monotonic anchor taken once per camera, from that camera's own first-seen source timestamp, so the difference between two events from the same camera is exactly the difference between their source timestamps and no clock step can reorder them relative to each other. A per-process anchor was tried first and was wrong: file-backed sources count from 0.0 per file while time.monotonic() counts from boot, so a replayed event landed one uptime in the past. Cross-camera comparison is therefore precise to when each camera's anchor was established, not to true simultaneity. Not NTP-corrected after the anchor is taken, so treat it as accurate to the anchor, not to the nanosecond.

source_timestamp.description: The camera source's own timeline for the same instant — time.monotonic() for a live RTSP camera, seconds-from-start-of-file for a replayed one. This is the timeline a clip's pts and the camera telemetry are on, so it is what correlates an event with its evidence. Meaningful only within one process run for one camera: it resets on restart and two cameras do not share an origin. Never sort or display on it. Optional and nullable — absent or null on an event produced before this field existed.

track_ids.description: Every salient track in view when this was captured — the scene, not the subject. Context and search material; not an identification of who the event is about, because on a busy camera it is most of the frame and it changes every frame.

subject_track_ids.description: Who this event is *about*, when that is knowable — the tracks a behaviour detector attributed it to. Absent for the six automatic triggers, which describe a scene rather than a subject, and for camera-level findings like tampering that have nobody to attribute. Absent and `[]` mean the same thing. Consumers grouping events into incidents must use this and not `track_ids`: keying on the scene's tracks produces a different group on every frame.

welfare.description: A vision-language model's opinion about this keyframe (spec §5) — never a detector's verdict, and never present unless the model reported at least one concern. Optional: omitted entirely, not an empty object, when there is nothing to report. An empty `{"concerns": [], "basis": ...}` would read as 'assessed, nothing found'; omission reads as 'not assessed' — the two are different facts and this field must not conflate them. Absent on any payload written before this field existed.

confidence.description: Deliberately not a float and never 'certain' — a single still frame cannot honestly support more than these two grades.

evidence.description: The model's own words about what in the frame prompted this concern. Never a substance name, dose, or clinical judgement for kind=medication — only what was observed.

evidence_stated.description: Whether `evidence` is the model's own text. False means the model named this concern and described nothing, and `evidence` then holds a fixed placeholder rather than an observation — render it as such, never as though the model had described what it saw. Optional and absent on payloads written before this field existed: treat an absent value as true, matching the producer's own default, since a build that could not make the distinction always wrote the model's own text.

basis.description: Where this welfare opinion came from, so a consumer can weigh it without a side channel or any tribal knowledge of which pipeline produced it. `single_frame_vlm` is a vision-language model's reading of one still frame and nothing else. `temporal_pose_vlm` is that same reading corroborated by a multi-second geometry state machine that watched a person go from upright, through a rapid descent, to horizontal, and stay down (spec §7) — strictly more evidence than the first, and a second value rather than a widening of it precisely so that every opinion already stored under `single_frame_vlm` keeps meaning exactly what it meant when it was written. This was a `const` of `single_frame_vlm` until a second source existed; a consumer that hard-coded that value will now reject a `temporal_pose_vlm` payload, and that is the correct failure — it is being handed evidence of a kind it has no handling for.
